stem: A passenger in an elevator feels the sensation of upward acceleration. Which receptor primarily detects this stimulus?

options.A: Macula of the saccule
options.B: Macula of the utricle
options.C: Crista of the semicircular canal
options.D: Organ of Corti in the cochlea
options.E: Dorsal cochlear nucleus in the pons

explanation: The utricle senses horizontal linear acceleration and the saccule senses vertical linear acceleration. The semicircular canals sense rotation.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Macula of the saccule
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: While a patient fixates on a target and turns his head to the right, his eyes smoothly move to the left. Which pathway connects the vestibular nuclei to the ocular motor nuclei for this reflex?

options.A: Lateral vestibulospinal tract
options.B: Medial vestibulospinal tract
options.C: Medial longitudinal fasciculus
options.D: Lateral lemniscus
options.E: Medial lemniscus

explanation: The vestibulo-ocular reflex runs from the superior and medial vestibular nuclei through the MLF to the CN III, IV and VI nuclei.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Medial longitudinal fasciculus
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: A sleep EEG shows sleep spindles and K-complexes. Which stage is this?

options.A: Stage N1
options.B: Stage N3
options.C: REM
options.D: Stage N2
options.E: Awake

explanation: Sleep spindles and K-complexes mark stage N2. N3 shows delta waves, and REM shows a low-voltage, high-frequency EEG.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Stage N2
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: CBIL: Sleep

stem: A man with a right lateral brainstem infarct has ptosis, miosis and anhidrosis on the right. Which additional finding is most likely?

options.A: Spastic hemiparesis involving the contralateral upper and lower extremities
options.B: Loss of vibration sense and proprioception on the contralateral side of the body
options.C: Impaired light touch and pinprick sensation on the contralateral side of the face
options.D: Loss of pain and temperature sensation on the contralateral side of the body
options.E: Sensorineural hearing loss accompanied by tinnitus in the ipsilateral ear

explanation: The sympathetic dilation fibers descend in the lateral brainstem next to the anterolateral system. A lesion damages both, causing ipsilateral Horner syndrome and contralateral loss of pain and temperature in the body.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Loss of pain and temperature sensation on the contralateral side of the body
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A newborn with failure to thrive later develops insatiable hunger, obsession with food and obesity (Prader-Willi syndrome). Dysfunction of which hypothalamic nucleus best explains the hunger?

options.A: Lateral nucleus
options.B: Arcuate nucleus only
options.C: Ventromedial nucleus
options.D: Mammillary bodies
options.E: Suprachiasmatic nucleus

explanation: The ventromedial nucleus is the satiety center. Its failure causes constant hunger and obesity. The lateral nucleus is the hunger center, and its loss causes starvation.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ventromedial nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Hypothalamus & Smell/Taste

stem: A 44-year-old man has a right occipital condyle fracture. A week later his tongue deviates to the right on protrusion with fasciculations. Which structure is injured?

options.A: Left hypoglossal motor nucleus in the medullary tegmentum
options.B: Right corticobulbar tract within the posterior internal capsule
options.C: Right hypoglossal nerve in the bony hypoglossal canal
options.D: Right vagus nerve traversing the posterior jugular foramen
options.E: Right glossopharyngeal nerve traversing the jugular foramen

explanation: The hypoglossal canal lies next to the occipital condyle. An LMN lesion makes the tongue deviate toward the weak side, with fasciculations.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right hypoglossal nerve in the bony hypoglossal canal
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 30-year-old woman has a new tumor in the temporal lobe. Visual field testing shows loss of the upper right quadrant of the visual field in both eyes. Which structure is most likely damaged?

options.A: Left optic tract
options.B: Right parietal optic radiations
options.C: Left temporal optic radiations
options.D: Left parietal optic radiations
options.E: Central optic chiasm

explanation: Meyer loop carries fibers from the inferior retina (superior visual field) through the temporal lobe. A left temporal lesion gives a right upper homonymous quadrantanopia. A parietal lesion would give a lower quadrantanopia instead.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left temporal optic radiations
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual System

stem: A 73-year-old man has a slight resting tremor of the left hand that disappears on finger-to-nose testing. He has ratchet-like rigidity and a slow, shuffling gait. Which cells have degenerated?

options.A: GABAergic neurons of the striatum and globus pallidus
options.B: Cholinergic neurons of the basal nucleus of Meynert
options.C: Dopaminergic neurons of the substantia nigra pars compacta
options.D: Glutamatergic neurons of the subthalamic nucleus of Luys
options.E: Inhibitory Purkinje cells of the cerebellar cortex

explanation: This is Parkinson disease: resting tremor, ratchet-like (cogwheel) rigidity, bradykinesia and shuffling gait. The loss is of dopaminergic cells in the substantia nigra pars compacta.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dopaminergic neurons of the substantia nigra pars compacta
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 55-year-old man has lancinating leg pains, an ataxic gait, and absent vibration sense. His small, irregular pupils do not constrict to light but constrict when he focuses on a near object. Which describes this finding?

options.A: Marcus Gunn pupil
options.B: Argyll Robertson pupil
options.C: Adie tonic pupil
options.D: Horner syndrome pupil
options.E: Hutchinson pupil

explanation: Argyll Robertson pupil (neurosyphilis/tabes dorsalis) shows light-near dissociation: no constriction to light, but constriction with accommodation.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Argyll Robertson pupil
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 52-year-old man with Parkinson disease starts a new drug and develops compulsive gambling and sudden sleep attacks. Which drug is most likely responsible?

options.A: Carbidopa
options.B: Pramipexole
options.C: Entacapone
options.D: Benztropine
options.E: Selegiline

explanation: Dopamine agonists (pramipexole, ropinirole) can cause impulse control disorders and sleep attacks.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Pramipexole
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: Which is the net effect of dopamine from the substantia nigra on the striatum?

options.A: Inhibits the direct pathway via D1 receptors and excites the indirect pathway via D2 receptors
options.B: Excites the direct pathway via D1 receptors and inhibits the indirect pathway via D2 receptors
options.C: Excites both the direct and indirect pathways through nonselective dopamine D1/D2 activation
options.D: Inhibits both the direct and indirect pathways through tonic hyperpolarizing dopamine release
options.E: Directly excites the subthalamic nucleus to increase pallidal inhibition of the motor thalamus

explanation: Dopamine excites the direct pathway through D1 and inhibits the indirect pathway through D2. Both effects facilitate movement.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Excites the direct pathway via D1 receptors and inhibits the indirect pathway via D2 receptors
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 25-year-old man has an epidural hematoma after head trauma. His right pupil is dilated and unreactive to light, but eye movements are still normal. Which of the following best explains the early pupillary finding?

options.A: Sympathetic fibers course superficially within the cavernous sinus segment of the carotid plexus
options.B: Parasympathetic fibers run superficially on the outside of CN III and are compressed first
options.C: Somatic motor fibers course peripherally within the midbrain tegmentum and are infarcted early
options.D: Retinofugal afferent fibers course superficially along the lateral aspect of the optic tract
options.E: Trochlear nerve fibers course externally along the free tentorial edge and are stretched early

explanation: Parasympathetic fibers lie on the outside of CN III, so compression (uncal herniation, PComm aneurysm) gives a dilated, unreactive pupil first, while the central somatic fibers keep eye movements normal.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Parasympathetic fibers run superficially on the outside of CN III and are compressed first
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 27-year-old man has paralysis of both legs below T9 after aortic surgery. He has hyperactive reflexes, bilateral upgoing toes and loss of pin-prick sensation. Vibration and light touch are intact. What are the most likely findings below the lesion?

options.A: Bilateral flaccid paralysis with loss of vibration sense and preserved pain sensation
options.B: Right spastic paralysis with loss of proprioception and preserved pain sensation
options.C: Bilateral spastic paraparesis with loss of pain and temperature sensation
options.D: Complete bilateral sensory and motor loss below the level of the spinal cord lesion
options.E: Preserved voluntary motor power with isolated bilateral loss of proprioception

explanation: Anterior spinal artery occlusion damages both lateral corticospinal tracts and the anterolateral system, but spares the dorsal columns (posterior spinal artery supply).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Bilateral spastic paraparesis with loss of pain and temperature sensation
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 30-year-old man has a stab wound causing right hemisection of the spinal cord at T8. Which pattern is expected below the lesion?

options.A: Left spasticity and vibration loss, with preserved pain and temperature sensation
options.B: Bilateral spastic paraparesis, with bilateral loss of pain and temperature sensation
options.C: Bilateral loss of vibration and proprioception, with intact voluntary motor power
options.D: Right spasticity and vibration loss, with left loss of pain and temperature sensation
options.E: Right flaccid paralysis and pain loss, with preserved left sensation and motor power

explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome: ipsilateral UMN signs and loss of vibration/proprioception below the lesion, contralateral loss of pain and temperature, and LMN signs at the lesion level.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right spasticity and vibration loss, with left loss of pain and temperature sensation
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 73-year-old man presents with a low-frequency resting pill-rolling tremor that is predominantly localized to his left hand and arm. Neurologic examination also reveals left-sided cogwheel rigidity and bradykinesia, consistent with early Parkinson disease. Which brain structure is primarily responsible for the pathophysiology of this patient's left-hand motor symptoms?

options.A: Right substantia nigra pars compacta
options.B: Left substantia nigra pars compacta
options.C: Left cerebellar dentate nucleus
options.D: Right cerebellar hemisphere cortex
options.E: Bilateral subthalamic nuclei equally

explanation: The basal ganglia loop acts on the ipsilateral motor cortex, which controls the contralateral body, so a left-hand tremor comes from the right substantia nigra.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right substantia nigra pars compacta
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 40-year-old man has atrophy and fasciculations of the right quadriceps and an absent right patellar reflex. Which spinal cord segments mediate the reflex that is absent?

options.A: C5–C6
options.B: S1–S2
options.C: L3–L4
options.D: L1–L2
options.E: S3–S4

explanation: The patellar reflex uses L3–L4. LMN signs include atrophy, fasciculations and decreased or absent reflexes.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: L3–L4
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 45-year-old woman can wrinkle her forehead and close both eyes, but the right corner of her mouth droops when she smiles. Where is the lesion most likely located?

options.A: Right peripheral facial nerve distal to the stylomastoid foramen
options.B: Left corticobulbar tract rostral to the pontine facial motor nucleus
options.C: Right facial motor nucleus within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.D: Right corticobulbar tract rostral to the pontine facial motor nucleus
options.E: Right cerebellopontine angle mass compressing cranial nerve VII

explanation: Sparing of the forehead and eye closure with lower-face weakness is a corticobulbar (UMN) pattern. The lesion is contralateral to the weak face, here on the left, above the facial nucleus in the caudal pons.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left corticobulbar tract rostral to the pontine facial motor nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 45-year-old woman with insomnia is prescribed a drug that blocks orexin receptors. Which drug is this?

options.A: Suvorexant
options.B: Zolpidem
options.C: Ramelteon
options.D: Zaleplon
options.E: Modafinil

explanation: Suvorexant is an orexin receptor antagonist. Ramelteon is a melatonin agonist, and zolpidem and zaleplon act at the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Suvorexant
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: CBIL: Sleep

stem: A 70-year-old man with Parkinson disease taking selegiline is started on fluoxetine for depression. He develops agitation, fever, tremor and diarrhea. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
options.B: Hepatotoxicity
options.C: Cheese reaction only
options.D: Serotonin syndrome
options.E: Dyskinesia

explanation: MAO-B inhibitors (selegiline, rasagiline) combined with serotonergic drugs can cause serotonin syndrome. They also cause the tyramine (cheese) effect.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Serotonin syndrome
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: An 82-year-old man has difficulty understanding high-pitched voices. Which region of the cochlea is preferentially affected in age-related hearing loss?

options.A: Basal turn of the cochlea
options.B: Apical turn of the cochlea
options.C: Middle turn of the cochlea
options.D: Membranous labyrinth vestibule
options.E: External osseous spiral lamina

explanation: Presbycusis affects high frequencies because hair cells at the base of the cochlea are lost first.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Basal turn of the cochlea
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: A 45-year-old factory worker has episodes of vertigo lasting about an hour, a buzzing sound in his left ear and a sense of fullness. A 512-Hz tuning fork test lateralizes to the right on Weber, and Rinne is positive in both ears. What type of hearing loss does he have?

options.A: Right conductive hearing loss
options.B: Left conductive hearing loss
options.C: Right sensorineural hearing loss
options.D: Left sensorineural hearing loss
options.E: Normal hearing

explanation: Weber lateralizes to the right (the good ear) and Rinne is normal (positive), so the left ear has sensorineural loss. Together with vertigo, tinnitus and fullness, this is Meniere disease.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left sensorineural hearing loss
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: A 47-year-old man has a toothache, fever, a swollen left eye with proptosis, an absent corneal reflex and limited eye movements. A thrombosis of the cavernous sinus is suspected. Which other nerve passes through this structure?

options.A: CN V3
options.B: CN V2
options.C: CN VII
options.D: CN IX
options.E: CN XII

explanation: The cavernous sinus contains CN III, IV, V1, V2 and VI. V3 exits through the foramen ovale and does not pass through it.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: CN V2
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 45-year-old factory worker presents with recurrent, episodic vertigo lasting about an hour per episode, accompanied by low-frequency buzzing tinnitus in his left ear and a persistent sensation of aural fullness. Tuning fork examination shows bone conduction greater than air conduction in neither ear, and the Weber test lateralizes to the right ear, consistent with left-sided sensorineural hearing loss. Which of the following best explains the underlying pathophysiologic mechanism of this patient's condition?

options.A: Excessive accumulation and elevated hydrostatic pressure of endolymph within the membranous labyrinth
options.B: Dislodgement and free-floating migration of otoconia into the posterior semicircular canal ampulla
options.C: Benign Schwann cell neoplasm originating along the vestibular division of cranial nerve VIII
options.D: Post-viral inflammatory demyelination selectively involving the superior vestibular nerve branch
options.E: Destructive expansion of keratinized stratified squamous epithelium within the middle ear cavity

explanation: Meniere disease is caused by excess endolymph increasing pressure in the endolymphatic space. Treatment is sodium restriction and diuretics.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Excessive accumulation and elevated hydrostatic pressure of endolymph within the membranous labyrinth
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: What is the mechanism of riluzole?

options.A: Free radical scavenger that decreases oxidative cellular damage
options.B: Presynaptic GABA-B agonist that increases spinal motor inhibition
options.C: Central alpha-2 adrenergic agonist that reduces spastic muscle tone
options.D: Presynaptic glutamate release inhibitor and NMDA receptor antagonist
options.E: Direct dopamine D2 receptor agonist that stimulates striatal pathways

explanation: Riluzole is an NMDA antagonist that reduces glutamate excitotoxicity. Edaravone is the free radical scavenger.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Presynaptic glutamate release inhibitor and NMDA receptor antagonist
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: CBIL: ALS

stem: A 78-year-old man with tremor-predominant Parkinson disease is considered for benztropine. What is the main concern in this patient?

options.A: Acute fulminant hepatic necrosis
options.B: Severe symptomatic orthostatic hypotension
options.C: Cognitive confusion and urinary retention
options.D: Hyperpyrexic serotonin syndrome crisis
options.E: Erythematous livedo reticularis rash

explanation: Anticholinergics (benztropine, trihexyphenidyl) help tremor but cause confusion, memory impairment, urinary retention and dry mouth, especially in the elderly.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Cognitive confusion and urinary retention
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 19-year-old woman cannot raise her left eyebrow, close her left eye or smile on the left. Which finding most strongly favors a lower motor neuron (Bell palsy) over a stroke?

options.A: Drooping of the lower face on the affected side
options.B: Deviation of the tongue on protrusion to the affected side
options.C: Preserved voluntary smiling on the affected side
options.D: Spastic hemiparesis involving the ipsilateral upper extremity
options.E: Inability to wrinkle the forehead on the affected side

explanation: Bell palsy (LMN) weakens the upper and lower face on the same side. Stroke spares the forehead because the upper face receives bilateral corticobulbar input.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Inability to wrinkle the forehead on the affected side
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 38-year-old man presents with progressive emotional lability, restlessness, cognitive decline, and sudden, involuntary, dance-like choreiform movements of his extremities. His father died in his mid-40s of a similar progressive neurodegenerative condition. Which of the following neuropathologic processes directly underlies the chorea observed in this patient?

options.A: Progressive loss of dopaminergic projection neurons within the substantia nigra
options.B: Degeneration of striatal GABAergic neurons in the indirect pathway disinhibiting the thalamus
options.C: Apoptosis of cerebellar Purkinje neurons leading to profound intention tremor
options.D: Focal ischemic cavitation within the contralateral subthalamic nucleus of Luys
options.E: Toxic hepatocellular and striatal copper accumulation with impaired ceruloplasmin

explanation: Loss of striatal GABAergic neurons (caudate and putamen) of the indirect pathway disinhibits the thalamus and causes chorea. The ventricles enlarge (hydrocephalus ex vacuo).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Degeneration of striatal GABAergic neurons in the indirect pathway disinhibiting the thalamus
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 72-year-old woman has rapidly progressive visual distortion and central vision loss. Fluorescein angiography shows neovascularization with subretinal bleeding. Which treatment is most appropriate?

options.A: Antioxidant vitamin supplements
options.B: Topical prostaglandin
options.C: Intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy
options.D: Oral acyclovir
options.E: Topical carbonic anhydrase inhibitor

explanation: Wet AMD involves neovascularization with bleeding and is treated with anti-VEGF. Antioxidant vitamins are for dry AMD (drusen).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Ophthalmology

stem: A 73-year-old man has a hand tremor and 3 years of kicking his wife during sleep, with no recall of it. The sleep disorder in this patient is most strongly associated with which pathology?

options.A: Neuronal alpha-synuclein aggregation
options.B: Trinucleotide CAG repeat expansion
options.C: Hyperphosphorylated TDP-43 inclusion bodies
options.D: Hepatolenticular copper accumulation
options.E: Extracellular amyloid-beta deposition

explanation: REM sleep behavior disorder can precede Parkinson disease and Lewy body dementia by years and reflects alpha-synuclein pathology.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Neuronal alpha-synuclein aggregation
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 35-year-old man wakes up and rolls onto his left side, and the room begins to spin for under a minute. He has no hearing loss or tinnitus. The Dix-Hallpike maneuver reproduces his symptoms with nystagmus. The curative maneuver for this condition works by doing which of the following?

options.A: Facilitating drainage of excess endolymphatic fluid through the endolymphatic duct
options.B: Increasing reflexive contraction of the stapedius and tensor tympani middle ear muscles
options.C: Relieving microvascular pulsatile compression along the root entry zone of cranial nerve VIII
options.D: Augmenting central vestibular compensation circuits within the medullary vestibular nuclei
options.E: Repositioning dislodged canalith otoconia out of the semicircular canal into the utricular vestibule

explanation: This is BPPV. The Epley maneuver moves the otoconia from the semicircular canal into the vestibule.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Repositioning dislodged canalith otoconia out of the semicircular canal into the utricular vestibule
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: A 62-year-old smoker has right ptosis, a small pupil and decreased sweating on the right side of his face, plus shoulder pain. Which pathway is most likely interrupted?

options.A: Preganglionic sympathetic fibers ascending over the lung apex to the superior cervical ganglion
options.B: Postganglionic parasympathetic pupillomotor fibers traversing the inferior branch of CN III
options.C: Preganglionic parasympathetic visceral motor neurons originating in the Edinger-Westphal nucleus
options.D: Postganglionic sympathetic sudomotor fibers descending along the external carotid plexus
options.E: Somatosensory primary afferent fibers traversing the ophthalmic division of cranial nerve V

explanation: This is Horner syndrome from a Pancoast tumor. Second-order preganglionic sympathetic fibers arise in the intermediolateral column and pass over the lung apex, then reach the superior cervical ganglion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Preganglionic sympathetic fibers ascending over the lung apex to the superior cervical ganglion
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 22-year-old man has a complete spinal cord transection at C2 after a diving accident. After the period of spinal shock, which of the following is expected?

options.A: Hyperactive patellar reflex and an intact spinal flexor withdrawal reflex
options.B: Absent patellar reflex and absent spinal flexor withdrawal reflex
options.C: Absent patellar reflex and hyperactive spinal flexor withdrawal reflex
options.D: Normal patellar reflex and absent spinal flexor withdrawal reflex
options.E: Hypoactive patellar reflex and flaccid tone with absent withdrawal reflex

explanation: The patellar and withdrawal reflexes use local spinal circuits and do not need the brain. After spinal shock, the patellar reflex is hyperactive because of the UMN lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Hyperactive patellar reflex and an intact spinal flexor withdrawal reflex
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 45-year-old man with a lumbar tumor has radicular leg pain, flaccid leg weakness with decreased reflexes, and saddle anesthesia. Which is the most likely site of injury?

options.A: Thoracolumbar anterior spinal artery territory
options.B: Hemisection of the thoracic spinal cord
options.C: Central canal syrinx within the cervical cord
options.D: Sacral cord segments of the conus medullaris
options.E: Lumbosacral nerve roots of the cauda equina

explanation: Cauda equina: lumbosacral roots give LMN signs, radicular pain and saddle anesthesia. A conus lesion gives bilateral UMN sacral signs and autonomic dysfunction.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Lumbosacral nerve roots of the cauda equina
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A hemiparetic stroke patient has a flexed arm and extended leg. Resistance to passive stretch is greatest at the start of the movement and increases with faster stretching. Which term describes this?

options.A: Rigidity
options.B: Spasticity
options.C: Flaccidity
options.D: Fasciculations
options.E: Chorea

explanation: Spasticity is velocity dependent, greatest at the start of passive movement, and shows flexor tone in the arm and extensor tone in the leg.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Spasticity
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: Which best explains bradykinesia in Parkinson disease?

options.A: Excessive excitatory thalamocortical drive by the ventral lateral thalamus
options.B: Widespread apoptotic loss of striatal GABAergic medium spiny neurons
options.C: Pathologic hyperactivation of the direct basal ganglia motor pathway
options.D: Complete functional failure of the glutamatergic subthalamic nucleus
options.E: Increased inhibitory GABAergic output of the internal globus pallidus to the thalamus

explanation: Dopamine loss weakens the direct pathway and strengthens the indirect pathway. GPi inhibition of the VL thalamus rises and cortical drive falls, causing bradykinesia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Increased inhibitory GABAergic output of the internal globus pallidus to the thalamus
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 62-year-old man has right arm weakness with increased tone, brisk reflexes and a Babinski sign 3 weeks after a stroke. Which mechanism best explains the increased tone and reflexes?

options.A: Direct excitotoxic apoptosis of spinal anterior horn alpha motor neurons
options.B: Selective denervation atrophy of intrafusal muscle spindle dynamic fibers
options.C: Impairment of retrograde neurotrophic transport in peripheral motor nerves
options.D: Autoimmune receptor blockade at the postsynaptic neuromuscular junction
options.E: Loss of descending inhibitory upper motor neuron input to spinal reflex arcs

explanation: UMN signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski) are release phenomena caused by loss of inhibitory input to lower motor neurons.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Loss of descending inhibitory upper motor neuron input to spinal reflex arcs
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 30-year-old woman with a spinal cord injury has a stiff, flexed right arm. Which drug reduces spasticity by activating alpha-2 receptors?

options.A: Baclofen
options.B: Tizanidine
options.C: Dantrolene
options.D: Cyclobenzaprine
options.E: Botulinum toxin

explanation: Tizanidine is an alpha-2 agonist that reduces norepinephrine drive on motor neurons. Baclofen is a GABA-B agonist.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Tizanidine
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: CBIL: ALS

stem: A 20-year-old man struck in the head has decreased facial sensation on the left and when he opens his mouth, his jaw deviates to the left. Which structure is injured?

options.A: Left trigeminal nerve root
options.B: Right trigeminal nerve root
options.C: Left facial nerve
options.D: Right corticobulbar tract
options.E: Left hypoglossal nerve

explanation: The left trigeminal root contains sensory and motor fibers. The unopposed right lateral pterygoid pushes the jaw toward the weak left side.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left trigeminal nerve root
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 66-year-old man has sudden, violent flinging movements of the left arm and leg after a lacunar stroke. Where is the lesion?

options.A: Left caudate nucleus
options.B: Left substantia nigra
options.C: Right subthalamic nucleus
options.D: Right putamen nucleus
options.E: Left subthalamic nucleus

explanation: Hemiballismus follows a subthalamic nucleus lesion and affects the contralateral side, so left-sided flinging indicates the right STN.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right subthalamic nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: A patient has a lesion of the right optic nerve. Which pupillary responses are expected?

options.A: Right eye light: left pupil constricts; left eye light: right pupil constricts
options.B: Right eye light: both pupils constrict; left eye light: neither pupil constricts
options.C: Right eye light: neither pupil constricts; left eye light: neither pupil constricts
options.D: Right eye light: right pupil constricts; left eye light: neither pupil constricts
options.E: Right eye light: neither pupil constricts; left eye light: both pupils constrict

explanation: Right optic nerve lesion: the afferent limb is lost on that side. Light in the right eye produces no response in either pupil, but light in the left eye constricts both pupils.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right eye light: neither pupil constricts; left eye light: both pupils constrict

stem: Which finding best distinguishes central vertigo from peripheral vertigo?

options.A: Intense fatigable vertigo with prominent hearing loss and tinnitus
options.B: Direction-fixed horizontal nystagmus that suppresses with visual fixation
options.C: Direction-changing nystagmus unsuppressed by fixation with limb ataxia and dysarthria
options.D: Brief episodic vertigo triggered by head position changes fading within 60 seconds
options.E: Isolated sudden-onset vertigo following an uncomplicated viral upper respiratory infection

explanation: Central vertigo is milder, not fatigable, and nystagmus is not suppressed by fixation, with other brainstem or cerebellar signs and no hearing loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Direction-changing nystagmus unsuppressed by fixation with limb ataxia and dysarthria
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: A 40-year-old man has vertical diplopia when walking downstairs. Which maneuver best tests the muscle that is weak?

options.A: Abduct the eye and ask the patient to look up
options.B: Abduct the eye and ask the patient to look down
options.C: Ask the patient to look straight ahead and converge
options.D: Adduct the eye and ask the patient to look up
options.E: Adduct the eye and ask the patient to look down

explanation: The superior oblique mainly depresses the eye when adducted. Ask the patient to adduct the eye and look down.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Adduct the eye and ask the patient to look down
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 30-year-old woman with right facial droop from Bell palsy also complains that ordinary sounds are painfully loud in her right ear. Paralysis of which muscle explains this?

options.A: Tensor tympani (CN V)
options.B: Stapedius (CN VII)
options.C: Tensor veli palatini (CN V)
options.D: Masseter (CN V)
options.E: Stylopharyngeus (CN IX)

explanation: The stapedius (CN VII) dampens stapes movement. Its paralysis in Bell palsy causes hyperacusis. The tensor tympani is supplied by CN V.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Stapedius (CN VII)
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: Because the central auditory pathway projects bilaterally, which single lesion would cause complete deafness in the right ear?

options.A: Right inferior colliculus
options.B: Left medial geniculate nucleus
options.C: Right transverse temporal gyrus
options.D: Right cochlear nuclei
options.E: Right lateral lemniscus

explanation: Central auditory pathways are bilateral, so most lesions above the cochlear nuclei cause little hearing loss (but impair localization). Only a cochlear nucleus lesion blocks all input from one ear.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right cochlear nuclei
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: A patient has an acute infarct of the right frontal eye field. In which direction do the eyes deviate?

options.A: Toward the right side of the lesion
options.B: Toward the left side away from the lesion
options.C: Directed upward toward the superior visual field
options.D: Directed downward toward the inferior visual field
options.E: Centered at midline with preserved convergence

explanation: After a stroke, the intact opposite FEF dominates, so the eyes look toward the lesion. A right FEF infarct deviates the eyes to the right.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Toward the right side of the lesion
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 53-year-old woman on carbamazepine for trigeminal neuralgia has confusion, headache and hyponatremia. Which hypothalamic nuclei produce the hormone responsible?

options.A: Arcuate and periventricular nuclei
options.B: Lateral and ventromedial nuclei
options.C: Anterior and posterior nuclei
options.D: Supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei
options.E: Suprachiasmatic and mammillary nuclei

high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Hypothalamus & Smell/Taste

stem: A 66-year-old man has a lacunar infarct in the left posterior limb of the internal capsule. What is the expected presentation?

options.A: Left hemiparesis with left lower facial weakness and hyperreflexia
options.B: Fluent aphasia with dense right superior homonymous quadrantanopia
options.C: Paraparesis with bilateral extensor plantar responses and sensory loss
options.D: Right hemiparesis with spasticity and right lower facial weakness
options.E: Contralateral hemi-sensory loss with complete preservation of motor power

explanation: The posterior limb of the internal capsule carries corticospinal and corticobulbar fibers, so a left lesion gives right hemiparesis, spasticity and lower facial weakness.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right hemiparesis with spasticity and right lower facial weakness
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 48-year-old woman has progressive leg stiffness with foot drag, increased tone, brisk Achilles reflexes, bilateral Babinski signs, normal sensation, and morning headaches with papilledema. Which area is most likely compressed?

options.A: Intramedullary mass compressing the cervical spinal cord dorsal columns
options.B: Subcortical glioma involving the posterior limb of the internal capsule
options.C: Parasagittal falcine meningioma compressing bilateral paracentral lobules
options.D: Degenerative mass compressing anterior horn cells of the lumbar enlargement
options.E: Ischemic lesion involving the medullary pyramids at the decussation

explanation: A parasagittal meningioma along the falx compresses both paracentral lobules (legs), giving bilateral leg UMN signs. Headache and papilledema indicate a mass.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Parasagittal falcine meningioma compressing bilateral paracentral lobules
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A man has a stroke that destroys the left lateral geniculate nucleus. Which of the following findings is most likely?

options.A: Left homonymous hemianopia with intact pupillary light reflexes
options.B: Bitemporal hemianopia with absent pupillary light reflexes
options.C: Right superior quadrantanopia with impaired pupillary accommodation
options.D: Left monocular blindness with an afferent pupillary defect
options.E: Right homonymous hemianopia with intact pupillary light reflexes

explanation: An LGN lesion gives a contralateral homonymous hemianopia. The pupillary light reflex is normal because the reflex fibers leave the optic tract before the LGN and go to the pretectal area.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right homonymous hemianopia with intact pupillary light reflexes
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual System

stem: A 50-year-old man has right-sided hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance and a constant mild headache for a year. MRI shows a mass at the right cerebellopontine angle. As the mass enlarges, which additional nerve is most likely to be affected?

options.A: CN IX
options.B: CN VII
options.C: CN XI
options.D: CN XII
options.E: CN IV

explanation: This is a vestibular schwannoma at the CPA. CN VII lies next to CN VIII, so facial involvement is common, and CN V may be affected as well.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: CN VII
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: A patient with spasticity and liver disease should avoid which peripherally acting agent that prevents calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum?

options.A: Baclofen
options.B: Tizanidine
options.C: Cyclobenzaprine
options.D: Botulinum toxin
options.E: Dantrolene

explanation: Dantrolene blocks calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum and is hepatotoxic, so avoid it in liver disease.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dantrolene
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: CBIL: ALS

stem: A 30-year-old man with a chronic spinal cord injury has rhythmic, repeated contractions of his calf when the foot is passively dorsiflexed. What explains this finding?

options.A: Intrinsic myofibrillar fatigue within fast-twitch gastrocnemius motor units
options.B: Denervation supersensitivity of postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
options.C: Intention tremor resulting from cerebellar dentatorubrothalamic tract dysfunction
options.D: Hyperactive stretch reflex circuitry resulting from loss of descending inhibition
options.E: Entrapment compression neuropathy affecting the distal tibial nerve in the tarsal tunnel

explanation: Clonus is repeated activation of a hyperactive stretch reflex after loss of descending inhibition, best seen at the ankle (S1–S2).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Hyperactive stretch reflex circuitry resulting from loss of descending inhibition
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 68-year-old man has a left posterior cerebral artery infarct and develops a right homonymous hemianopia. Fixation testing shows that central vision is preserved. Which of the following best explains this macular sparing?

options.A: Exclusive projection of macular visual streams to the contralateral lateral geniculate nucleus
options.B: Complete bypass of primary occipital striate cortex by ascending geniculocalcarine fibers
options.C: Selective decussation of central foveal photoreceptor axons at the central optic chiasm
options.D: Dual collateral blood supply and large occipital pole cortical representation of the macula
options.E: Collateral visual representation within tertiary sensory association areas of the parietal lobe

explanation: The macula has a large cortical representation and a second arterial supply, so it is typically spared by a PCA infarct. Trauma with large lesions can remove this sparing.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dual collateral blood supply and large occipital pole cortical representation of the macula
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual System

stem: A 58-year-old man has right hemiparesis and his tongue deviates to the left on protrusion. Which lesion best explains this combination?

options.A: Right internal capsule posterior limb
options.B: Left precentral motor cortex hand area
options.C: Right medial medulla oblongata
options.D: Left medial medulla oblongata
options.E: Right midbrain cerebral peduncle

explanation: A left medial medullary lesion damages the left CN XII (tongue deviates left) and the left pyramid (right hemiparesis). The tongue deviates opposite the body weakness: an alternating hemiplegia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left medial medulla oblongata
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 28-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis has double vision on left gaze. On looking left, her left eye abducts but her right eye stays at midline. Convergence is intact. Where is the lesion?

options.A: Left medial longitudinal fasciculus
options.B: Left paramedian pontine reticular formation
options.C: Right abducens motor nucleus
options.D: Right oculomotor motor nucleus
options.E: Right medial longitudinal fasciculus

explanation: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia. On left gaze the left abducens fires but the right MLF cannot carry the signal to the right oculomotor nucleus, so the right eye does not adduct. Convergence is preserved because it bypasses the MLF.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right medial longitudinal fasciculus
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 60-year-old man is treated for Pseudomonas pneumonia with tobramycin and furosemide. He develops bilateral tinnitus and hearing loss. Which structures are most likely injured?

options.A: Ossicles
options.B: Tympanic membrane
options.C: Semicircular canal cupula only
options.D: Eustachian tube
options.E: Cochlear hair cells

explanation: Aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, cisplatin and salicylates damage cochlear hair cells and cause sensorineural loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Cochlear hair cells
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: A 50-year-old strict vegan has paresthesias, loss of vibration sense, spastic weakness and hyperreflexia. Which tracts are involved?

options.A: Anterolateral spinothalamic tracts and anterior horn alpha motor neurons
options.B: Posterior dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal descending motor tracts
options.C: Anterior and posterior spinocerebellar ascending sensory tracts
options.D: Anterior corticospinal motor tracts and medial longitudinal fasciculi
options.E: Dorsolateral tracts of Lissauer and dorsal horn substantia gelatinosa

explanation: B12 deficiency (subacute combined degeneration) damages the dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Posterior dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal descending motor tracts
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A patient has loss of taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue (CN VII), posterior third (CN IX) and epiglottis (CN X). Where do these first-order taste fibers synapse?

options.A: Ventral posteromedial nucleus of the thalamus
options.B: Gustatory portion of the solitary nucleus
options.C: Primary gustatory cortex within the insula
options.D: Primary olfactory cortex within the uncus
options.E: Branchial motor neurons of the nucleus ambiguus

explanation: CN VII, IX and X taste fibers synapse in the solitary nucleus, then project to the VPM thalamus and the insula/postcentral gyrus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Gustatory portion of the solitary nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Hypothalamus & Smell/Taste

stem: A 75-year-old man takes an alpha-1 blocker for BPH. During cataract surgery, his pupil is unusually small. Which mechanism is most likely?

options.A: Antagonism of alpha-1 adrenergic receptors on the pupillary dilator muscle
options.B: Direct pharmacologic stimulation of parasympathetic postganglionic fibers in CN III
options.C: Selective excitotoxic destruction of cholinergic neurons in the Edinger-Westphal nucleus
options.D: Competitive antagonism of muscarinic M3 receptors on the pupillary sphincter muscle
options.E: Direct alpha-2 adrenergic stimulation suppressing central pretectal sympathetic outflow

explanation: The pupillary dilator is sympathetic (norepinephrine on alpha-1 receptors). An alpha-1 blocker relaxes it, leaving the constrictor unopposed and the pupil small.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Antagonism of alpha-1 adrenergic receptors on the pupillary dilator muscle
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A reflex hammer taps the patellar tendon and the quadriceps contracts. Which receptor initiates this reflex?

options.A: Muscle spindle
options.B: Golgi tendon organ
options.C: Pacinian corpuscle
options.D: Free nerve ending
options.E: Meissner corpuscle

explanation: The muscle spindle senses stretch and sends Ia afferents to alpha motor neurons in a two-neuron reflex arc.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Muscle spindle
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 60-year-old woman enters a dark movie theater and develops a painful red left eye, headache, nausea and halos around lights. The eye feels hard. Which mechanism best explains the attack?

options.A: Excessive active secretion of aqueous humor by the bilayered ciliary body epithelium
options.B: Neovascular proliferation across the anterior chamber angle inducing synechial closure
options.C: Accumulation of extracellular drusen material beneath the retinal pigment epithelium
options.D: Mydriasis-induced apposition of the iris against the trabecular meshwork outflow tract
options.E: Cross-linking and oxidative aggregation of crystallin proteins in the crystalline lens

explanation: Acute angle-closure glaucoma is precipitated by pupillary dilation (dim light, drugs), which pushes the iris against the iridocorneal angle. Cholinomimetics treat it by constricting the pupil.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Mydriasis-induced apposition of the iris against the trabecular meshwork outflow tract
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Ophthalmology

stem: A 35-year-old man with chronic fat malabsorption reports difficulty seeing in dim light. A deficiency of vitamin A most directly impairs the synthesis of which of the following?

options.A: Cone opsins in the fovea only
options.B: Rhodopsin in rods
options.C: Melanin in the RPE
options.D: Neurotransmitter in bipolar cells
options.E: Aqueous humor

explanation: Vitamin A is needed to synthesize rhodopsin and cone opsins. Rods (rhodopsin, peripheral retina, dim light) fail first, producing night blindness.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Rhodopsin in rods
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual System

stem: A 46-year-old woman must now hold her menu at arm's length to read it. Her distance vision is normal. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism?

options.A: Shortened axial length of the globe focusing near images behind the retina
options.B: Elongated axial length of the globe focusing distant images in front of the retina
options.C: Age-related loss of crystalline lens elasticity and decreased ciliary curvature change
options.D: Asymmetrical irregular curvature of the anterior corneal refracting surface
options.E: Separation of the posterior vitreous humor cortex from the internal limiting membrane

explanation: Presbyopia is age-related stiffening of the lens, so near images focus behind the retina. Hyperopia (eye too short) and myopia (eye too long) are not age-related changes.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Age-related loss of crystalline lens elasticity and decreased ciliary curvature change
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual System

stem: A 30-year-old woman has brief episodes of an unpleasant burning smell followed by lip smacking. Which structure is most likely the seizure focus?

options.A: Uncus of the temporal lobe
options.B: Occipital pole striate cortex
options.C: Postcentral gyrus sensory cortex
options.D: Vermis of the cerebellum
options.E: Frontal eye field motor cortex

explanation: Uncinate seizures arise in the uncus (primary olfactory cortex) and cause olfactory hallucinations, often unpleasant odors.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Uncus of the temporal lobe
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Hypothalamus & Smell/Taste

stem: A 38-year-old man has mood swings, restlessness, sudden jerking of the left arm that he disguises as purposeful, and a father who died at age 45. What is the genetic basis of this condition?

options.A: CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion in the HTT gene on chromosome 4
options.B: ATP7B loss-of-function copper transport mutation on chromosome 13
options.C: SOD1 superoxide dismutase missense mutation on chromosome 21
options.D: Microdeletion of the paternal 15q11-q13 region on chromosome 15
options.E: CTG trinucleotide repeat expansion in the DMPK gene on chromosome 19

explanation: Huntington disease: autosomal dominant CAG expansion in HTT on chromosome 4. More repeats mean earlier onset in successive generations (anticipation).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion in the HTT gene on chromosome 4
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 19-year-old has a seizure focus in the right frontal eye field. In which direction do the eyes deviate during the seizure?

options.A: Toward the right
options.B: Directly upward
options.C: Fixed in the midline
options.D: Toward the left
options.E: Directly downward

source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 61-year-old man has levodopa-induced dyskinesia. Which drug can reduce dyskinesia?

options.A: Levodopa
options.B: Ropinirole
options.C: Benztropine
options.D: Haloperidol
options.E: Amantadine

high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Amantadine
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: In the auditory pathway, which structure receives the output of the inferior colliculus before the signal reaches the cortex?

options.A: Ventral posteromedial thalamic nucleus
options.B: Medial geniculate nucleus
options.C: Lateral geniculate nucleus
options.D: Ventral posterolateral thalamic nucleus
options.E: Superior olivary complex

explanation: The order is cochlear nuclei, superior olive, lateral lemniscus, inferior colliculus, medial geniculate nucleus, and then Heschl gyrus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Medial geniculate nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: A 24-year-old woman with a history of narcolepsy experiences frequent, disabling episodes of sudden bilateral muscle weakness and collapse provoked by laughter (cataplexy), as well as distressing sleep paralysis and hypnagogic hallucinations. In addition to daytime scheduled naps and modafinil for somnolence, which of the following medications is most effective for suppressing REM sleep and controlling her cataplexy?

options.A: Modafinil
options.B: Zolpidem
options.C: Venlafaxine
options.D: Haloperidol
options.E: Pramipexole

explanation: SSRIs and SNRIs (such as venlafaxine) suppress REM sleep and reduce cataplexy, hallucinations and sleep paralysis. Modafinil treats daytime sleepiness.

stem: A 14-year-old boy has headaches and cannot look upward. A mass is found near the third ventricle. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism?

options.A: Neoplastic compression of the abducens motor nucleus in the dorsal caudal pons
options.B: Demyelinating plaque involving the medial longitudinal fasciculus in the pons
options.C: Pineal gland germinoma compressing the dorsal midbrain pretectal area
options.D: Pituitary macroadenoma compressing crossing decussating fibers in the optic chiasm
options.E: Ischemic lacunar stroke involving the paramedian pontine reticular formation

source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 50-year-old man is brought in by a friend after several recent car accidents. Visual field testing shows loss of vision in the temporal half of the visual field of both eyes. Which of the following fibers are most likely compressed?

options.A: Temporal retinal fibers from both eyes

options.C: Optic tract fibers on one side
options.D: Optic radiations on one side
options.E: Temporal retinal fibers from the right eye only

stem: Which gene is most associated with familial ALS?

options.A: HTT
options.B: ATP7B
options.C: SOD1
options.D: SNCA
options.E: PMP22

stem: A 35-year-old woman has a cape-like loss of pain and temperature over both shoulders and arms, but preserved light touch. She also has weakness and atrophy of the hands. Which structures are most likely damaged?

options.A: Anterior white commissure decussating fibers of the spinothalamic tracts
options.B: Cervical fasciculus cuneatus sensory axons within the posterior columns
options.C: Lateral corticospinal descending motor tracts within the lateral funiculus
options.D: Lumbosacral primary motor and sensory nerve roots of the cauda equina
options.E: Dorsal root entry zone fibers traversing the tract of Lissauer

stem: A 7-year-old girl screams for several minutes nightly, is inconsolable and has no memory of it in the morning. In which stage does this occur?

options.A: REM sleep
options.B: NREM stage N3
options.C: NREM stage N2
options.D: NREM stage N1
options.E: Sleep onset latency

stem: A patient with a lesion of the left nucleus ambiguus is asked to say "ah." Which of the following findings is expected?

options.A: Uvula deviation to the left with loss of the right-sided pharyngeal gag reflex
options.B: Uvula deviation to the right with loss of the left-sided pharyngeal gag reflex
options.C: Tongue deviation to the left with contralateral spastic hemiparesis of the body
options.D: Tongue deviation to the right with contralateral spastic hemiparesis of the body

stem: An 18-year-old college student presents with excessive daytime somnolence, falling asleep repeatedly during lectures and social conversations. She reports vivid, frightening visual hallucinations upon falling asleep, transient inability to move upon awakening in the morning, and sudden episodes of bilateral knee buckling and facial drooping provoked by laughter or surprise while remaining fully conscious. Which of the following diagnostic studies is best to definitively confirm the suspected diagnosis?

options.B: Contrast-enhanced brain MRI evaluating for hypothalamic structural lesions

stem: A 58-year-old man reports flashes, floaters and a curtain descending over his right eye. Which mechanism explains the photoreceptor damage?

options.A: Elevated intraocular pressure inducing ischemic optic nerve head cupping and axonal death
options.B: Separation of the neurosensory retina from the underlying retinal pigment epithelium and choroid

stem: Which drug treats chorea in Huntington disease?

options.A: Levodopa

options.B: Benztropine

stem: A 52-year-old man develops chills and shivering on an 85°F day and has a temperature of 103°F. He also has bitemporal hemianopia. Which hypothalamic structure is most likely involved?

options.A: Lateral nucleus
options.B: Ventromedial nucleus
options.C: Suprachiasmatic nucleus
options.D: Posterior nucleus
options.E: Anterior nucleus

explanation: Anterior nucleus lesion: the posterior (heating) nucleus acts unopposed, causing fever, chills and shivering. Bitemporal hemianopia fits a lesion near the chiasm.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Anterior nucleus

stem: A 60-year-old man with open-angle glaucoma starts a new eye drop and notices longer, darker eyelashes. Which is the mechanism of this drug?

options.A: Decreases active aqueous humor secretion by the nonpigmented ciliary epithelium
options.B: Increases uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humor through the ciliary muscle
options.C: Induces pupillary constriction and opens the trabecular meshwork via muscarinic drive
options.D: Inhibits carbonic anhydrase enzymes responsible for bicarbonate and aqueous production
options.E: Antagonizes presynaptic alpha-2 adrenergic receptors to reduce sympathetic outflow

explanation: Prostaglandin analogs increase uveoscleral outflow and cause eyelash growth. Beta-blockers, alpha-agonists and diuretics reduce production.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Increases uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humor through the ciliary muscle
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Ophthalmology

stem: A 25-year-old man has progressive night blindness and loss of peripheral vision. His family has a similar history, and an ERG is abnormal. Which pathologic change underlies the abnormal ERG?

options.A: Progressive apoptotic degeneration of rod and cone photoreceptor cells
options.B: Extracellular accumulation of drusen deposits beneath the retinal epithelium
options.C: Impaired trabecular meshwork drainage causing elevated ocular pressure
options.D: Mechanical separation of the neurosensory layer from the choroidal vascular bed
options.E: Progressive stromal edema causing loss of optical corneal transparency

explanation: Retinitis pigmentosa is a family of inherited photoreceptor degenerations. The ERG, a recording of phototransduction, is abnormal because photoreceptors are lost.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Progressive apoptotic degeneration of rod and cone photoreceptor cells
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Ophthalmology

stem: An 18-year-old woman falls asleep in class, has vivid hallucinations as she falls asleep, cannot move for a minute on waking, and collapses when startled while remaining conscious. What is the underlying pathology?

options.A: Histaminergic neurons of the tuberomammillary nucleus
options.B: Orexin-producing neurons of the lateral hypothalamus
options.C: GABAergic neurons of the ventrolateral preoptic nucleus
options.D: Melatonin-sensitive neurons of the suprachiasmatic nucleus
options.E: Serotonergic neurons of the median and dorsal raphe nuclei

explanation: This is narcolepsy with cataplexy, sleep paralysis and hypnagogic hallucinations. It is caused by loss of orexin (hypocretin) neurons in the lateral hypothalamus (HLA-DQB1\*0602).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Orexin-producing neurons of the lateral hypothalamus
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: CBIL: Sleep

stem: Which of the following is typically spared in ALS?

options.A: Extraocular motility and urinary bladder control
options.B: Tongue protrusion and pharyngeal swallowing coordination
options.C: Upper extremity distal intrinsic hand motor strength
options.D: Diaphragmatic contraction and intercostal ventilation
options.E: Proximal shoulder abduction and neck flexion power

explanation: ALS spares sensation, extraocular movements, and bowel and bladder function.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Extraocular motility and urinary bladder control

stem: A 62-year-old woman has had progressive, painless loss of central vision in her right eye over the past year. The left eye is normal. The lesion is most likely located in which of the following?

options.A: Left optic tract
options.B: Central optic chiasm
options.C: Right lateral geniculate nucleus
options.D: Left visual cortex
options.E: Right optic nerve

explanation: A monocular deficit means the lesion is anterior to the chiasm, in the right optic nerve or retina. Anything behind the chiasm produces a bilateral (homonymous) defect.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right optic nerve
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual System

stem: A patient with a right spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) lesion will have which of the following deficits?

options.A: Weak left shoulder shrug and weak head turn to the right
options.B: Weak left shoulder shrug and weak head turn to the left
options.C: Weak right shoulder shrug and weak head turn to the right
options.D: Bilateral shoulder shrug weakness with intact bilateral head turn
options.E: Weak right shoulder shrug and weak head turn to the left

explanation: CN XI supplies the trapezius and sternocleidomastoid. The right SCM turns the head to the left, so a right lesion weakens the right shrug and leftward head turn.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Weak right shoulder shrug and weak head turn to the left
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: UMN/LMN

stem: A 56-year-old man with Parkinson disease is prescribed levodopa with carbidopa. Why is carbidopa added?

options.A: It penetrates the central nervous system to augment striatal dopamine synthesis
options.B: It selectively blocks postsynaptic D2 dopamine receptors in the limbic system
options.C: It inhibits peripheral dopa decarboxylase without crossing the blood-brain barrier
options.D: It selectively and irreversibly inhibits central monoamine oxidase type B
options.E: It stimulates calcium-dependent vesicular dopamine release from terminal axons

explanation: Carbidopa does not cross the blood-brain barrier. It blocks peripheral dopa decarboxylase, so more levodopa reaches the CNS at a lower dose with less nausea.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It inhibits peripheral dopa decarboxylase without crossing the blood-brain barrier
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 63-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension has sudden diplopia. His right eye is positioned down and out with ptosis. Both pupils are equal and reactive to light. Which is the most likely cause?

options.A: Posterior communicating artery saccular aneurysm compression
options.B: Transtentorial uncal herniation mass effect compression
options.C: Microvascular ischemic infarct of the oculomotor nerve
options.D: Superior cervical ganglion sympathetic chain disruption
options.E: Medial longitudinal fasciculus demyelinating plaque

explanation: An ischemic CN III infarct (diabetes, hypertension) causes ptosis and an eye down and out, with the pupil spared because the superficial parasympathetic fibers are not affected.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Microvascular ischemic infarct of the oculomotor nerve
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: Which transmitter and receptor mediate sympathetic stimulation of sweat glands?

options.A: Norepinephrine at alpha-1 receptors
options.B: Norepinephrine at beta-2 receptors
options.C: Dopamine at D1 receptors
options.D: Epinephrine at beta-1 receptors
options.E: Acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors

explanation: Sweat glands are the sympathetic exception. Postganglionic fibers release acetylcholine onto muscarinic receptors.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors

stem: A 20-year-old with liver disease and behavior changes has a flapping, wing-beating tremor and Kayser-Fleischer rings. What is the defect?

options.A: Trinucleotide repeat expansion in the HTT gene on chromosome 4
options.B: Superoxide dismutase 1 missense mutation on chromosome 21
options.C: Abnormal alpha-synuclein misfolding and Lewy body aggregation
options.D: ATP7B copper-transporting ATPase gene mutation on chromosome 13
options.E: Hereditary HFE gene missense mutation causing excessive iron absorption

explanation: Wilson disease: ATP7B defect on chromosome 13 causes copper accumulation (liver, basal ganglia, Kayser-Fleischer rings) and a wing-beating tremor. Treat with copper chelation.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: ATP7B copper-transporting ATPase gene mutation on chromosome 13
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia

stem: A patient has a lesion of the right oculomotor nerve. Which pupillary responses are expected?

options.A: Right eye light: left pupil constricts; left eye light: left pupil constricts
options.B: Right eye light: both pupils constrict; left eye light: both pupils constrict
options.C: Right eye light: right pupil constricts; left eye light: right pupil constricts
options.D: Right eye light: neither pupil constricts; left eye light: neither pupil constricts
options.E: Right eye light: both pupils constrict; left eye light: left pupil constricts

explanation: A right CN III lesion removes the efferent limb on the right. The right pupil does not constrict to light in either eye, while the left pupil constricts normally.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right eye light: left pupil constricts; left eye light: left pupil constricts
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: What is the resting eye position after an acute lesion of the left paramedian pontine reticular formation (PPRF)?

options.A: Conjugate deviation of both eyes toward the left
options.B: Skew deviation with hypotropia of the left eye
options.C: Monocular medial resting deviation of the left eye
options.D: Conjugate resting deviation of both eyes downward
options.E: Conjugate deviation of both eyes toward the right

explanation: The PPRF drives the ipsilateral lateral rectus and contralateral medial rectus. A left PPRF lesion leaves the right side unopposed, so both eyes deviate to the right.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Conjugate deviation of both eyes toward the right
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 6-month-old infant has a dense unilateral cataract. Why is prompt surgery recommended?

options.A: Progressive intumescence of the infant lens will rapidly precipitate pupillary block glaucoma
options.B: Capsular micro-perforation will release lens crystallins and trigger phacolytic endophthalmitis
options.C: Congenital pediatric cataracts carry an immediate high risk of malignant retinoblastoma transformation
options.D: Total visual deprivation will induce rapid ischemic coagulation necrosis of the distal optic nerve
options.E: Deprivation of visual input during early critical development causes permanent cortical amblyopia

explanation: Cortical visual circuits develop in the first year. Unbalanced input from the two eyes causes permanent deficits, including blindness.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Deprivation of visual input during early critical development causes permanent cortical amblyopia

stem: A 40-year-old woman has slowly progressive hearing loss in her left ear. The Weber test lateralizes to the left ear, and on the left, bone conduction is louder than air conduction. Which is the most likely finding?

options.A: Right sensorineural hearing loss
options.B: Left sensorineural hearing loss
options.C: Left conductive hearing loss
options.D: Right conductive hearing loss
options.E: Bilateral presbycusis

explanation: In conductive loss, Weber lateralizes to the bad ear and Rinne is negative (bone louder than air) on that side.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left conductive hearing loss
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: A 28-year-old woman recovering from influenza wakes with continuous severe spinning vertigo, nausea and vomiting that last for days, along with hearing loss in her right ear. MRI is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
options.B: Endolymphatic hydrops (Meniere disease)
options.C: Acute isolated vestibular neuritis
options.D: Acute infectious labyrinthitis
options.E: Vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma)

explanation: Labyrinthitis follows a viral infection and gives days of continuous vertigo with hearing loss. BPPV is brief and positional, and Meniere is episodic.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Acute infectious labyrinthitis
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Auditory & Vestibular

stem: A 57-year-old man has dysphagia, tongue atrophy, hand weakness, brisk reflexes on one side, diminished reflexes on the other, and a left extensor plantar response. Sensation is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Myasthenia gravis
options.B: Primary lateral sclerosis
options.C: Progressive muscular atrophy
options.D: Cervical myelopathy
options.E: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis

explanation: Combined UMN signs (hyperreflexia, spasticity, Babinski) and LMN signs (tongue atrophy, hyporeflexia) with intact sensation indicate ALS. Primary lateral sclerosis is UMN only, and progressive muscular atrophy is LMN only.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: CBIL: ALS

stem: A 24-year-old man trips over his dog repeatedly when it is on his right side. MRI shows a lesion in the left parietal white matter. Which visual field deficit is most likely?

options.A: Right inferior homonymous quadrantanopia
options.B: Right superior homonymous quadrantanopia
options.C: Left inferior homonymous quadrantanopia
options.D: Bitemporal hemianopia
options.E: Left homonymous hemianopia

explanation: Superior (parietal) radiations carry the superior retina (inferior visual field) to the cuneus. A left parietal lesion gives a right inferior homonymous quadrantanopia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right inferior homonymous quadrantanopia
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual System

stem: A 25-year-old man fell off a truck and has extensive bilateral occipital lobe damage with cortical blindness. Which findings are most likely?

options.A: Absent pupillary light reflex; intact pupillary accommodation to visual near targets
options.B: Absent pupillary light reflex; absent pupillary accommodation to visual near targets
options.C: Intact pupillary light reflex; intact pupillary accommodation to visual near targets
options.D: Intact pupillary light reflex; absent pupillary accommodation to visual near targets
options.E: Intact pupillary light reflex; paradoxical pupillary dilation to visual near targets

explanation: The light reflex runs retina to pretectal area to Edinger-Westphal, bypassing the cortex, so it is normal. Accommodation needs the visual cortex, so it is lost to a visual stimulus, but voluntary convergence still produces miosis.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Intact pupillary light reflex; absent pupillary accommodation to visual near targets
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 35-year-old man has a resting tremor, rigidity and postural instability after starting a new medication. Which drug most likely caused this?

options.A: Levodopa
options.B: Diazepam
options.C: Sumatriptan
options.D: Haloperidol
options.E: Pyridostigmine

explanation: Dopamine D2 blockers (haloperidol, metoclopramide) cause drug-induced parkinsonism. Levodopa treats Parkinson disease rather than causing it.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Haloperidol
source: USMLE Step 1 Replicate Bank: Basal Ganglia
